newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran building $30 million car plant on Gulf island.
newsitem.headline: Iran building $30 million car plant on Gulf island.

text.p: Iran has started building a car plant worth $30 million in its free-trade zone on the Gulf island of Kish, a newspaper said on Saturday.

The dailly Iran said the Kish Khodro factory, to be built at a cost of 90 billion rials ($30 million at the official exchange rate), was expected to be completed by March 1998. Construction work began on Thursday.
It would have an annual production capacity of 5,000 multi-purpose vehicles, it added.
French carmaker Renault SA signed an agreement last month with Kish Khodro to deliver mechanical parts for the vehicles, including 1.6-litre engines and gear boxes. The terms were not disclosed.

Fifty-one percent of Kish Khodro shares are held by private investors, 40 percent by an Iranian state bank and the rest by BMS Management, a British engineering group which designed the vehicle, Renault said.
Kish is one of three free-trade zones on the Gulf set up by Iran in 1989 to draw foreign investment to rebuild its economy after the 1980-88 war with Iraq.
($1 = 3,000 rials at the official exchange rate)
